rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. This config tests RNA-only singleprofile with PCA encoding, isolating RNA modality performance. It clarifies if RNA data alone can achieve competitive accuracy, providing foundational evidence for future multimodal comparisons.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only singleprofile with PCA achieves 0.48 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile RNA with PCA and avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation. It balances exploration of multiprofile (which may capture more data diversity) and exploitation of PCA (used in the baseline). This comparison directly addresses whether multiprofile improves accuracy, a key design choice with high uncertainty.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002) outperform singleprofile ones. This experiment tests replacing pca_n2000 with scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated encoder) while retaining avgpool aggregation (from config_002). This isolates the effect of RNA encoder quality, a critical design choice, and builds on the promising multiprofile direction with minimal changes.

Existing evidence shows rna_only multiprofile models with scvi_n200 encoder (config_005: 0.65 accuracy) outperform pca_n2000 (config_002: 0.59). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool (used in config_005) with transformer aggregation improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It builds on the promising scvi_n200 encoder while exploring a key design choice with minimal parameter changes.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve 0.653 accuracy. This experiment tests combining scvi_n200 (best RNA encoder) with resnet50 (strong image encoder) in a multimodal setup, using avgpool aggregation and concat fusion. It isolates the effect of multimodal integration while leveraging proven components, balancing exploration of multimodal potential with exploitation of existing high-performing elements.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6529). This experiment tests scgpt encoder with transformer aggregation in multiprofile setting, isolating the effect of RNA encoder choice while keeping aggregation consistent. It balances exploration (testing new encoder) and exploitation (building on successful aggregation method).

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy (0.653). This experiment tests combining this RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder and transformer aggregation using concat fusion, to evaluate if multimodal approaches can surpass the current RNA-only best. It isolates the effect of adding image modality while keeping RNA and aggregation methods consistent with prior success.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder (e.g., config_032) achieve the highest accuracy (0.6878). This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion in the same setup improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It is the best use of the remaining budget to refine the top-performing configuration.

The existing evidence shows that config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy so far (0.724989). This experiment tests whether using scgpt as the RNA encoder (instead of scvi_n200) with the same image encoder, aggregation, and fusion settings could further improve performance. It clarifies the impact of RNA encoder choice on multimodal performance, leveraging the strong image encoder and fusion strategy already validated in config_039.

The existing evidence shows config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy of 0.724989. This experiment tests whether using avgpool aggregation instead of transformer aggregation (with weighted fusion) maintains high performance, clarifying the impact of aggregation methods. It is the best use of the final experiment to validate if a simpler aggregation method could match or exceed the current best, balancing exploration of critical design choices.
